messages.author: 4a35c9df8f85dadc
messages.subject: error for projected occupancy
parts:
Hello,
I am running a multiseason analysis in unmarked and am interested in
your recommendations for reporting error on occupancy projections
(using projected() ). It seems that you could get estimates of SE via
the Delta Method using the estimates and SE's of initial occ, col, and
ext along with the recursive occupancy equation, but I'm not sure if
this is the best route. Any suggestions or information would be
appreciated.

Thanks,
Brittany Mosher

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] error for projected occupancy
parts:
The example on the colext help page hints at how to get bootstrapped
SEs for the derived estimates of psi. Here is a little more detail
following the example:

example(colext)

fm <- nonparboot(fm, B = 100) # This takes a while! And in practice B
should be >>100

psi.proj <- f...@projected.mean[1,]
psi.proj.se <- f...@projected.mean.bsse[1,] # This is the boot strap
standard error

# Plot estimates and SE bars
plot(psi.proj, ylim=c(0.1, 0.3))
segments(1:7, psi.proj-psi.proj.se, 1:7, psi.proj+psi.proj.se)


The delta method is an option too, but it is not implemented yet for
this specific case.

of the Google Group. The spam filter sends them to me first, so it's
better if you join.

Richard

Hi Richard and unmarked group,

I am bringing this old post by Brittany back up, because I have a similar question. I am trying to project second season occupancy (I only have two seasons) and understand how to use nonparboot(), but I am trying to break the projected occupancy and error down by treatment. I have 4 treatments and want the projected occupancy and SE for each treatment for both seasons. I can get the projected occupancy for each treatment, but it seems the non-parametric bootstrap method only gives out a SE for the mean occupancy across all of my sites.

an example model would be:
test <- colext(psiformula=~as.factor(trt), gammaformula=~as.factor(trt), epsilonformula=~as.factor(trt), pformula=~covariate, data=umf)

Any help would be great.

Travis

Hi Travis,

You could use predict() to give you estimates of treatment-specific psi (for year 1), gamma, and epsilon, which you could then use to calculate treatment-specific psi for year 2. If you package this up as a function, you could then use parboot to give you SEs and CIs. Make sense? 

Richard

Hi Richard,

So I am having difficulty getting my function into a "fitted model inheriting class unmarkedFit" for nonparaboot. When I run nonparaboot with my function I get the following error.

Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  : 
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘nonparboot’ for signature ‘"numeric"’

I am assuming that ti because my function creates a vector of estimates and is no tin the unmarkedFit class. Below is the code the function I wrote. Thanks again!

###CODE###
treatment<- data.frame(trt=seq(1,4,1))
treatment

y2 = function(treatment){
predict.trt<-colext(psiformula = ~as.factor(trt), gammaformula = ~as.factor(trt), epsilonformula = ~as.factor(trt), 
                    pformula = ~gust, data = umf)

#predict psi by treatment
predict.psi.trt <- predict(predict.trt, type="psi", newdata=treatment, appendData=TRUE)
psi=c(predict.psi.trt[1,1],predict.psi.trt[2,1],predict.psi.trt[3,1],predict.psi.trt[4,1])

#predict col by treatment
predict.col.trt <- predict(predict.trt, type="col", newdata=treatment, appendData=TRUE)
col=c(predict.col.trt[1,1],predict.col.trt[2,1],predict.col.trt[3,1],predict.col.trt[4,1])

#predict ext by treatment
predict.ext.trt <- predict(predict.trt, type="ext", newdata=treatment, appendData=TRUE)
ext=c(predict.ext.trt[1,1],predict.ext.trt[2,1],predict.ext.trt[3,1],predict.ext.trt[4,1])

psi.2=NULL

for (i in 1:4){
psi.2[i] = psi[i]*(1-ext[i]) + (1-psi[i])*col[i]
    }
return(psi.2)
}
y2(treatment)

nonparboot(y2(treatment),B=10)

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] error for projected occupancy
parts:
Hi Travis,

I suggest using parboot instead of nonparboot for this. Your function might look something like this:

f <- function(fm) {
  psi1.hat <- predict(fm, type="psi", newdat=treatment)[,1]
  gamma.hat <- predict(fm, type="col", newdat=treatment)[,1]
  eps.hat <- predict(fm, type="ext", newdat=treatment)[,1]
  psi2.hat <- psi1.hat*(1-eps.hat) + (1-psi1.hat)*gamma.hat
  return(psi2.hat)
}

pb <- parboot(fm1, statistic=f, nsim=1000) # fm1 is the name of you fitted model object

It's late in the day on Friday, so it's possible I botched this. Also, I'm guessing that your treatment variable should be coded as a factor instead of a numeric variable. 

Richard

On Monday, September 27, 2010 at 12:26:12 PM UTC-6, Richard Chandler wrote:
The example on the colext help page hints at how to get bootstrapped
SEs for the derived estimates of psi. Here is a little more detail
following the example:

example(colext)

fm <- nonparboot(fm, B = 100)  # This takes a while! And in practice B
should be >>100

psi.proj <- f...@projected.mean[1,]
psi.proj.se <- f...@projected.mean.bsse[1,] # This is the boot strap
standard error

# Plot estimates and SE bars
plot(psi.proj, ylim=c(0.1, 0.3))
segments(1:7, psi.proj-psi.proj.se, 1:7, psi.proj+psi.proj.se)


The delta method is an option too, but it is not implemented yet for
this specific case.
